newsitem.title: INDIA: India Arvind to raise denim output.
newsitem.headline: India Arvind to raise denim output.

text.p: Arvind Mills Ltd, one of the world's top denim makers, is raising its production of denim by 50 percent, managing director Sanjay Lalbhai said.
It is expanding capacity to make an additional 40 million metres of denim by March 1997. It currently makes 80 million metres of denim. The expansion will cost 2.0-2.5 billion rupees.
"We've a dream to make Arvind a truly global textile conglomerate," he told reporters on Saturday. "We plan to expand through acquisitions and mergers." He did not give details.
The company has susbsidiaries in the U.S., Germany, Hong Kong and Mauritius and exports to 75 countries.
The firm is also setting up facilities to make knit-wear and other fabrics.
Lalbhai said it is investing 2.0 billion rupees in a 40 megawatt plant to generate its own electricity, which will insulate it from irregular power supply and higher costs.

Arvind Mills expects to increase its turnover to 11 billion rupees in the financial year ending March 31, 1997, from 8.44 billion in 1995/96, B.M. Shah, vice president, corporate finance, told Reuters.

Lower cotton prices this year will help the company improve its gross margins to 20 percent after it fell to 11 percent in 1995/96, Lalbhai said, adding that it was increasing its presence in the branded segment.
The company is raising one billion rupees through a domestic debenture issue to fund capital expenditure and to retire short-term loans.
The firm raised $125 million in January 1994 through an issue of global depositary receipts and is listed on the London and Luxembourg bourses.
